verdict.suspectedIssue: Bulk discount (minQty 4, 10% off) appears not to be applied independently of the promo code. In turn 1 the cart had 4 items (2×house-blend, 1×single-origin, 1×cold-brew-kit, subtotal $90.00), which meets the bulkDiscount minQty of 4, yet the only discount shown was $9.00 attributed to BREW10 (total $81.00). If bulk and promo stack, the total should be $72.90; more importantly, if the bulk rule applies at all on its own, a 4-item cart with NO promo code must total $81.00, not $90.00. The single observation cannot distinguish 'bulk silently skipped' from 'intentionally non-stacking', so confirmation requires the same cart without any promo code.
verdict.evidenceSummary: Turn 1 mixed cart (qty 4, subtotal 9000 minor) with BREW10 showed discountMinor 900 and promoStatus 'BREW10 applied: 10% off' — no separate line or evidence of the catalog's bulkDiscount rule (minQty 4, 10% off) being applied even though the cart quantity threshold was met. Turn 2 quantity change behaved correctly (1450→2900 for qty 1→2). Price display and cart-count checks all passed.

repair.diagnosis: Off-by-one in the bulk discount threshold in totals(): the condition uses count > bulkDiscount.minQty, so a cart of exactly 4 items never qualifies. The rule requires minQty 4 (i.e., 4 or more), so bulk discount is silently skipped for the confirmed 4-item cart.
repair.evidenceSummary: Cart 2×house-blend (2×1450) + 1×single-origin (2200) + 1×cold-brew-kit (3900) = subtotal 9000 minor, count = 4. With promoPercent 0 the code path afterBulk = bulk && count > 4 ? ... : subtotal evaluates false, so discount = 0 and total = 9000, matching observedTotalMinor 9000. Correct total per catalog rule is 9000 × 0.9 = 8100.
repair.rationale: Single-token fix aligning the comparison with the rule's minimum-quantity semantics (minQty 4 means ≥ 4). With the fix and no promo code, the confirmed scenario totals 8100 ($81.00); with BREW10 it stacks correctly (9000 − 900 bulk − 810 promo = 7290). Only allowed pricing file app.js is touched; 'old' occurs exactly once; no execution/process/shell code; catalog values are not hardcoded (rule still read from window.CATALOG).
